# WORKFLOW REDESIGN SPECIFICATION
## Process-Based Navigation with Advanced Mode Toggle

**Status:** Design Requirements Document  
**Date:** May 2, 2026  
**Purpose:** Transform navigation from category-based to process-based, with optional advanced mode

---

## 1. NAVIGATION REDESIGN OVERVIEW

### Current Structure (Category-Based) ❌
```
Foundation
├─ Overview
├─ Identity
└─ Research

Tasks & Tracking
├─ Tasks
├─ Notes
└─ Playtest Reports

Workshop
├─ Components
└─ Players

Rules & Flow
├─ Rules
├─ Rulebook
├─ Turn Structure
└─ Layout

Simulation
├─ Simulator
├─ Scaling
├─ Scoring Curve
└─ Balance

Playtesting
├─ Sessions
├─ Calendar
├─ Feedback
└─ Reports

Exports
Learning
Collaboration
```

## 2. COMPONENT SPECIFICATIONS

```
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Behaviors:**
- [ ] Sticky (always visible)
- [ ] Shows game name, player count, duration, type
- [ ] Shows completion percentage (calculated from stages)
- [ ] Collapse button hides to single-line header
- [ ] Click game name to edit identity
- [ ] Click completion % to see checklist

**Advanced Mode Toggle:**
- [ ] In header, right side
- [ ] When OFF (default): Show only current stage + next 2 stages
- [ ] When ON: Show all 6 stages, all tabs visible

## 4. STAGE UNLOCK LOGIC

### Completion Calculation

```
Stage Completion % = (Completed Checklist Items / Total Items) * 100

Stage 1 Checklist:
  ✅ Name game (1)
  ✅ Choose players (1)
  ✅ Set duration (1)
  ⏳ Pick genre (1)
  ⏳ Research (optional - doesn't count)
  
  Completed: 3/4 = 75% → Can unlock Stage 2

Unlock Rule:
  - Show "Ready for Stage 2?" button when ≥ 70%
  - Allow jump to Stage 2 when unlocked
  - Show warning if jumping early
```

### Lock/Unlock Behaviors

- [ ] Stage 1 always unlocked (starting stage)
- [ ] Stage N unlocked when Stage N-1 ≥ 70%
- [ ] Can override lock in Advanced Mode (show warning)
- [ ] Can return to any previous stage
- [ ] Can pause a stage and come back


## 6. ADVANCED MODE SPECIFICATION

### Toggle Location & Behavior

```
Header: [Normal Mode] [Advanced Mode ▼]
```

**When Normal Mode (Default):**
- [ ] Show only current stage + 2 next stages
- [ ] Hide all tabs except current stage tabs
- [ ] Show checklists and guidance
- [ ] Show "Next Step" prompts
- [ ] Sidebar collapses on mobile
- [ ] Right sidebar shows Design Advisor

**When Advanced Mode:**
- [ ] Show all 6 stages in sidebar
- [ ] Show all tabs under each stage
- [ ] Hide checklists and guidance
- [ ] Hide "Next Step" prompts
- [ ] Sidebar expanded
- [ ] Right sidebar shows Design Advisor + Chat only
- [ ] Allow jumping to any stage (no locks)

**Toggle State:**
- [ ] Persists in localStorage
- [ ] User preference remembered
- [ ] Show "first-time" tooltip when mode switches

---

## 7. MOBILE RESPONSIVENESS

### Layout Rules

**Small Screens (<768px):**
- [ ] Header: Single line, game name + %, Advanced toggle
- [ ] Sidebar: Icon-only (left hamburger menu)
- [ ] Stage panel: Full width
- [ ] Right sidebar: Bottom drawer or hidden
- [ ] Progress bar: Horizontal scroll or collapsed

**Medium Screens (768px - 1024px):**
- [ ] Header: Full
- [ ] Sidebar: Collapsed by default, expandable
- [ ] Stage panel: 70% width
- [ ] Right sidebar: Hidden by default, toggleable
- [ ] Progress bar: Full

**Large Screens (>1024px):**
- [ ] Header: Full
- [ ] Sidebar: Always visible
- [ ] Stage panel: 60% width
- [ ] Right sidebar: Always visible
- [ ] Progress bar: Full

---

## 8. INTERACTION SPECIFICATIONS

### Navigation Actions

| Action | Normal Mode | Advanced Mode |
|--------|------------|----------------|
| Click stage name | Jump to stage (if unlocked) | Jump to stage |
| Click tab | Show tab content | Show tab content |
| Collapse header | Minimize to 1-line | N/A |
| Expand right panel | Always visible | Toggle |
| Back button | Return to current stage | Return to current tab |
| Keyboard shortcuts | Alt+N = next step | Alt+# = stage # |

### Tab Transitions

- [ ] Sticky header remains visible
- [ ] Game brief context preserved
- [ ] Design Advisor updates for new tab
- [ ] Save form data before leaving tab
- [ ] Show "Unsaved changes" warning if navigating away

---

## 9. DATA & STATE MANAGEMENT

### What Gets Saved

```
Navigation State:
├─ currentStage (1-6)
├─ currentTab (per stage)
├─ isAdvancedMode (boolean)
├─ sidebarCollapsed (boolean)
└─ rightPanelCollapsed (boolean)

Game State:
├─ All game data (as before)
├─ Stage completion (calculated %)
├─ Unlock status per stage
└─ Design Advisor results

User Preferences:
├─ advancedMode toggle
├─ sidebarWidth
└─ theme
```

### Persistence

- [ ] Navigation state in localStorage
- [ ] Game data in database (no change)
- [ ] Design Advisor results cached (24 hr)
- [ ] Playtest snapshots per stage

---

## 10. CONVERSION: NORMAL → ADVANCED

### When User Switches to Advanced Mode

```
┌─ ADVANCED MODE ────────────┐
│                            │
│ You're switching to        │
│ Advanced Mode. This        │
│ removes guidance and       │
│ allows skipping stages.    │
│                            │
│ You can switch back        │
│ anytime from the header.   │
│                            │
│ [Continue to Advanced]     │
│ [Stay in Normal Mode]      │
└────────────────────────────┘
```

**Changes on Switch:**
- [ ] Sidebar expands to show all 6 stages
- [ ] All tabs become visible (no locks)
- [ ] Checklists hide
- [ ] Guidance prompts disappear
- [ ] "Next Step" prompts hide
- [ ] Right sidebar simplifies

**Reverse Switching:**
- [ ] Can switch back to Normal Mode anytime
- [ ] No data loss
- [ ] Same game state preserved
- [ ] User stays on current tab

**Game Overview Step:**
```
GAME OVERVIEW
Define what your game is about.

YOUR GAME'S NAME
Choose a memorable name. You can change it anytime.
Example: "Spell Collector", "Tide Pools", "The Last Station"

PLAYERS
How many people will play?
2-4 is good for starting. You can test different counts later.

DURATION
How long does a game take?
45 minutes is a good starting point. Balance games often take longer.

GENRE
What's the feel of your game?
Cooperative = Players work together
Competitive = Players compete
Hybrid = Mix of both
```

**Game Brief Step:**
```
MECHANIC FINGERPRINT
Rate your game across 5 dimensions.

LUCK (Random vs. Deterministic)
High luck games: Dice rolling, card draws
Low luck: Pure strategy (like chess)

STRATEGY (Simple vs. Complex)
High strategy: Many decisions, branching paths
Low strategy: Limited choices

INTERACTION (Solitary vs. Engaging)
High interaction: Players affect each other
Low interaction: Parallel play (everyone does their own thing)

COMPLEXITY (Easy vs. Deep)
High complexity: Long rules, high learning curve
Low complexity: Pick up in 5 minutes

THEME (Immersive vs. Abstract)
High theme: Story, flavor, narrative
Low theme: Abstract mechanics (numbers on cards)
```

## 16. ERROR STATES & EDGE CASES

### Lock Warning

**When trying to jump to locked stage:**
```
⚠️ STAGE LOCKED

You need to complete 70% of Stage 1 
before moving to Stage 2.

Current Progress: 35%
Missing:
- [ ] Set game duration (5 min)
- [ ] Pick genre (2 min)
- [ ] Add reference games (optional)

```

### Incomplete Stage Navigation

```
⚠️ YOU'RE LEAVING EARLY

If you leave now, you can return anytime.

Remaining Steps:
- [ ] Set duration
- [ ] Pick genre

```

```
│ [Help]                 │
```

### Keyboard Navigation

```
Tab:         Move between elements
Shift+Tab:   Move back
Enter:       Activate button/tab
Space:       Toggle checkbox
Alt+N:       Next step
Alt+1-6:     Jump to stage 1-6
Esc:         Close modal/menu
```

### Screen Reader Support

- [ ] Stage headers: `<h2>`
- [ ] Tabs: `role="tablist"`
- [ ] Locked stages: `aria-disabled="true"`
- [ ] Progress: `aria-label="35% complete"`
- [ ] Buttons: Clear labels (not "Click here")

### Color Accessibility

- [ ] Stage colors have sufficient contrast (WCAG AA)
- [ ] Don't rely on color alone (use icons + labels)
- [ ] Lock icon for locked stages (not just color)

---

## 18. TESTING REQUIREMENTS

### Unit Tests

- [ ] Stage completion calculator
- [ ] Lock/unlock logic
- [ ] Mode toggle (Normal ↔ Advanced)
- [ ] Progress calculation

### Integration Tests

- [ ] Navigation between stages
- [ ] Data persistence across tabs
- [ ] Design Advisor updates on tab change
- [ ] Mobile menu behavior

### User Testing

- [ ] 5 new users, Normal Mode (first 60 min)
- [ ] 5 experienced users, Advanced Mode
- [ ] Mobile usability (iOS + Android)
- [ ] Completion rate per stage

### Success Criteria

- [ ] 100% completion of Stage 1 test users
- [ ] 80%+ find "Next Step" helpful
- [ ] <5 min to first saved component
- [ ] No confusion between tabs

---

This specification transforms Board-Game-Forge from a category-based tool (30 tabs, overwhelming) into a **process-based workflow** where:

1. **Normal Mode (Default):** Guided 6-stage process, checklists, "next steps" prompts
2. **Advanced Mode:** All tabs visible, no locks, no guidance
3. **Progression:** Clear path from concept → playable in 60 min
4. **Context:** Game brief always visible (sticky header)
5. **Guidance:** Design Advisor central, not hidden

**Key Metric:** Time to first playable game: 120+ min → 60 min

WHAT WORKS (The Good)
1. ✅ BASIC CARD CREATION (A Grade)
What I see:
[New Card Form]
├─ Name: [Spell Bolt] ✓
├─ Subtype: [Spell ▼] ✓ (predefined list)
├─ Effect: [Deal 5 damage]
├─ Flavor: [A flash of arcane power...]

[AI Generate Cards ✨]

Prompt: [Create 50 spell cards for a cooperative RPG...]
Count: [5 ▼]
[Generate]

✅ Lightning Bolt (Spell) — Deal 5 damage to 1 enemy

[Use All] [Use Selected] [Regenerate] [Discard]

✅ Can describe what I want in plain English

Grade: A- — Solid. Only issue: regenerate loses my edits.

3. ✅ PROPERTIES & STATS (B Grade)

Token → [Value]

✅ Auto-populated templates per card type
✅ Can add custom properties beyond templates

✅ Property defaults (Cost = 2, Power = 1, etc.)
✅ Can see all properties in a list

Grade: B — Good system, but hard to find. Buried in tabs.

❌ Not visible when adding cards (form only shows name, subtype, description)
❌ Have to navigate to separate "Properties" tab to add stats
❌ No inline editing (click to see list, can't edit on card directly)

counters, requires, spawns, upgrades, drops,
part-of, enables, enemy-of, ally-of, is-a

✅ Predefined verbs (counters, requires, etc.)
✅ Can link entities explicitly

Grade: B — Good for linking, but rarely used.

```sql
-- Workspace Management
CREATE TABLE workspaces (
  id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR(255),
  owner_id INT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP,
  plan VARCHAR(50), -- free, team, enterprise
  max_members INT,
  features JSONB  -- sso, ip_allowlist, audit_export, etc.
);

-- Fine-Grained Roles
CREATE TABLE roles (
  id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  workspace_id INT,
  name VARCHAR(100),
  description TEXT,
  permissions JSONB,  -- {view: [...], edit: [...], delete: [...]}
  custom BOOLEAN,     -- true if user-created, false if built-in
  created_by INT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP
);

-- Member Management
CREATE TABLE workspace_members (
  id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  workspace_id INT,
  user_id INT,
  role_id INT,
  status VARCHAR(50), -- active, suspended, invited
  invite_token VARCHAR(255),
  invited_by INT,
  invited_at TIMESTAMP,
  accepted_at TIMESTAMP,
  last_active_at TIMESTAMP
);

-- Audit Logging
CREATE TABLE audit_log (
  id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  workspace_id INT,
  user_id INT,
  action VARCHAR(50),  -- create, update, delete, share, view
  entity_type VARCHAR(50),  -- card, rule, project, user, etc.
  entity_id INT,
  changes JSONB,  -- before/after values
  ip_address VARCHAR(45),
  user_agent TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP,
  INDEX (workspace_id, created_at),
  INDEX (user_id, created_at)
);

-- Conflict Resolution
CREATE TABLE edit_conflicts (
  id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  workspace_id INT,
  project_id INT,
  entity_type VARCHAR(50),
  entity_id INT,
  user_a_id INT,
  user_b_id INT,
  user_a_change JSONB,
  user_b_change JSONB,
  status VARCHAR(50),  -- pending, merged, reverted, negotiated
  resolution JSONB,
  created_at TIMESTAMP,
  resolved_at TIMESTAMP
);

-- Session Management
CREATE TABLE sessions (
  id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INT,
  workspace_id INT,
  token VARCHAR(255),
  ip_address VARCHAR(45),
  user_agent TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP,
  last_active_at TIMESTAMP,
  expires_at TIMESTAMP,
  INDEX (user_id, workspace_id)
);

-- Feedback & Approvals
CREATE TABLE feedback_items (
  id INT PRIMARY KEY,

  entity_type VARCHAR(50),

  requester_id INT,
  approver_id INT,

  status VARCHAR(50),  -- pending, approved, rejected, discussed

  resolved_at TIMESTAMP
);
```

This is a 140-hour, 7-week enterprise collaboration overhaul split across two audiences:

- **Designer experience**: dashboard, unified inbox, conflict resolution, metrics, rich comments
- **CTO/Admin experience**: workspace management, audit log, fine-grained roles, session security, analytics

| Feature | Exists | Status |

| Share dialog + invite | ✅ | Working |
| Comments + @mentions + threads | ✅ | Working |

| Team analytics | ❌ | Doesn't exist |

---

## The Critical Architecture Decision

Before writing a single component, there's a fork in the road:

**Most of the features in this spec require new backend infrastructure** — not just new React components. The frontend is the small part. The audit log, conflict resolution, session management, fine-grained permissions, and workspace management all need database tables, API endpoints, and WebSocket events that don't exist yet.

The spec includes a database schema (good) but glosses over the hard parts:

### The Hard Parts

**1. Conflict Resolution** — The spec describes OT (Operational Transformation), the same technology Google Docs uses. Figma spent years on it. The "two people edit the same card" problem has three real solutions ranked by complexity:

- **Checkout/lock model** (2 days): User A opens a card → card is locked. User B sees "Randy is editing." Simple, no merge needed. Linear, Notion drafts, Google Docs offline all do this.
- **Last-write-wins + notification** (1 week): What you have now, but with a pop-up. "Your change was overwritten by Sarah — here's what changed."
- **OT/CRDT** (2–3 months): True concurrent editing with automatic merge. The full spec vision. This is a product in itself.

I'd recommend the checkout model for now. 80% of the conflict spec's value, 5% of the complexity.

**2. Fine-grained permissions** — Entity-level permissions ("can edit this specific card") require middleware to enforce on every API call. That's invasive to retrofit. Section-level permissions (can edit Cards section, can view Rules section) are achievable and cover 95% of use cases.

**3. Audit log** — Clean to implement if you add a log-writer middleware on the API side. Reads as a table with filters on the frontend. Backend work is a week; frontend is 2 days.

**4. SSO/IP allowlist/2FA** — They're using Clerk for auth. Clerk Pro already supports SAML SSO, MFA enforcement, and session management. This isn't code to write — it's a Clerk plan upgrade and configuration. Don't build it from scratch.

**5. SOC2** — Not a code feature. It's an audit process, policies, access controls, and evidence gathering. It takes 6–12 months. Don't include it in a development timeline.

---

## How I Would Implement It

### Phase 1: Frontend-only wins (Week 1–2, ~30 hours)
Build on data that already exists. No new API needed.

**CollaborationDashboard** — Aggregate existing presence, activity feed, and notifications into a single panel. The data is already there; it's just scattered across three different components. This delivers the "see who's online + what's pending" experience immediately.

**UnifiedInbox** — Merge comments mentioning you + activity items + notification bell into one scrollable list, grouped by type. Existing APIs, new presentation.

**Enhanced ActivityFeed** — Add context links ("Sarah edited Spell Bolt's Cost → 2") instead of flat text.

### Phase 2: Workspace + members (Week 3, ~15 hours)
This likely needs minor backend additions (workspace record, member metadata).

**WorkspaceSettings** — Member list, basic role management (upgrade the existing 4 roles to include custom labels), invite management. The ShareDialog shell already exists; this is an expanded version of it.

**PermissionMatrix** — Visual read-only table showing what each role can do. No new enforcement logic, just documentation UI.

### Phase 3: Audit log (Week 4, ~10 hours backend + 8 hours frontend)
Add an API middleware that writes to an `audit_events` table on every mutating request. Frontend is a filterable table — straightforward.

### Phase 4: Feedback & approvals (Week 5, ~20 hours)
Add a `feedback_items` table + API. This is the "request feedback from Sarah on this card" workflow. The comments system already handles the discussion part; feedback items layer approval/rejection states on top.

**FeedbackWidget** — Shows on each entity (card, rule). "Request Review" button → creates a feedback item → Sarah sees it in UnifiedInbox.

### Phase 5: Conflict detection (Week 6, ~15 hours)
Implement the **checkout model**, not OT. When a user opens an entity for edit, set an `edit_lock` with a 5-minute TTL. Other users see a banner: "Randy is editing this card." When Randy saves or navigates away, lock releases. Store the lock in Redis or as a row in the DB with `locked_by` + `locked_until`.

### Phase 6: Session management (Week 7, ~10 hours)
Via Clerk's existing session APIs. The backend exposes active sessions; the frontend renders a table with "Force logout" buttons. Clerk handles the actual token invalidation.

---

## What I'd Skip or Defer

| Feature | Why |
|---|---|
| IP allowlist | Clerk Pro feature, not custom code |
| SAML/SSO | Clerk Pro feature, configure not build |
| SOC2 | Not a code deliverable |
| OT/CRDT conflict resolution | Checkout model covers the real use case |
| Entity-level permissions | Section-level is 95% of the value |
| "Team health" AI alerts | Nice-to-have, needs data first |

---

## Realistic Timeline

Taking the spec's scope but with the right scoping decisions above:

| Phase | What | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CollaborationDashboard + UnifiedInbox | 2 weeks |
| 2 | Workspace settings + PermissionMatrix | 1 week |
| 3 | Audit log (backend + frontend) | 1.5 weeks |
| 4 | Feedback & approvals | 1.5 weeks |
| 5 | Conflict checkout model | 1 week |
| 6 | Session management (via Clerk) | 0.5 week |
| **Total** | | **~7.5 weeks** |

That's close to the spec's 7-week estimate but with a more honest scope. The spec's estimate assumed the hard things (OT, SOC2, entity-level permissions) were straightforward — they're not.

---

## My Recommendation Before Coding

1. **Confirm backend availability** — Are the API endpoints listed in the spec being built in parallel, or do I need to stub them? The frontend alone is ~60 hours of the 140. The backend is 80.

2. **Decide on conflict strategy** — Checkout/lock or OT? This decision determines 3 weeks of work.

3. **Verify Clerk plan** — If the workspace is on Clerk Pro, SSO/MFA/session management is a config change, not code. Worth checking before building it.

4. **Start with Phase 1** — CollaborationDashboard and UnifiedInbox can be built entirely from existing API data and will deliver immediate visible value while the backend work happens in parallel.
